lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: asking for clarification without hedging

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic asking for clarification without hedging task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner reads a provided fictional, genuinely ambiguous workplace instruction, first drafts the hedging version they might naturally write ('sorry to bother you, this is probably a dumb question, but maybe...'), then rewrites it as a direct, respectful clarification request.
safetyNotes: The unclear instruction is fictional and provided with this lesson.
materials: learner-local: the provided fictional unclear instruction

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g10-u03-l03-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g10-u03-l03-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g10-u03-l03-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g10-u03-l03-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain, in your own words, the difference between a direct message and a rude one, using your own rewrite as the example.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g10-u03-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g10-u03-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g10-u03-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Removal of hedging language: Most hedging language is removed. | Clarity of the actual ask: States what's unclear and what's needed, though one could be sharper. | Distinguishing direct from disrespectful: Explanation correctly distinguishes direct from disrespectful with a general reason. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u03-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner write a version of the same clarification request for a much more time-sensitive situation, and explain what changes when urgency is added without losing respect.

resources.title: asking for clarification without hedging worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner reads a provided fictional, genuinely ambiguous workplace instruction, first drafts the hedging version they might naturally write ('sorry to bother you, this is probably a dumb question, but maybe...'), then rewrites it as a direct, respectful clarification request.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact asking for clarification without hedging decision or action.
Model move 2: Read the unclear instruction and write down, honestly, the hedging version you might naturally send.
Model move 3: Rewrite it as a direct, respectful clarification request that states exactly what's unclear and what you need.

Model check: Removal of hedging language: Most hedging language is removed. | Clarity of the actual ask: States what's unclear and what's needed, though one could be sharper. | Distinguishing direct from disrespectful: Explanation correctly distinguishes direct from disrespectful with a general reason.

resources.title: asking for clarification without hedging action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for asking for clarification without hedging.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: asking for clarification without hedging coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner reads a provided fictional, genuinely ambiguous workplace instruction, first drafts the hedging version they might naturally write ('sorry to bother you, this is probably a dumb question, but maybe...'), then rewrites it as a direct, respectful clarification request.
Coach direction: Read the unclear instruction and write down, honestly, the hedging version you might naturally send.
Learner prompt: Write your natural, hedging first-draft version, including any apologizing or self-doubting language you'd genuinely include.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: asking for clarification without hedging complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Rewrite it as a direct, respectful clarification request that states exactly what's unclear and what you need.
Response 1 (t2-p1): My rewrite removes unnecessary apologizing or self-doubting phrases.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My rewrite states exactly what part of the instruction is unclear.
Response 3 (t2-p3): My rewrite states exactly what I need to move forward (a specific answer or decision).
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: asking for clarification without hedging minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain, in your own words, the difference between a direct message and a rude one, using your own rewrite as the example.

Success checks: Removal of hedging language: Most hedging language is removed. | Clarity of the actual ask: States what's unclear and what's needed, though one could be sharper. | Distinguishing direct from disrespectful: Explanation correctly distinguishes direct from disrespectful with a general reason.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: asking for clarification without hedging supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g10-u03-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g10-u03-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional asking for clarification without hedging condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Removal of hedging language: Most hedging language is removed. | Clarity of the actual ask: States what's unclear and what's needed, though one could be sharper. | Distinguishing direct from disrespectful: Explanation correctly distinguishes direct from disrespectful with a general reason..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u03-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
